Calyx · frozen research · no live changes

Does a strong-dollar conflict veto help gold?

Five unchanged gold presets. One predeclared DXY filter. The original native trades are kept or vetoed; no new parameters are selected from these outcomes. This is an historical trade-subset screen, not a new native filtered-EA backtest.

Research-only, not deployed. All figures normalize each historical position to a fixed $100 initial-stop risk on a $10,000 reference: 1% of initial capital, no compounding. Fractional lots are unrestricted; broker lot minimums, margin and portfolio guards are not simulated. This is not a tradable-account or FTMO phase result.

Primary test: unchanged → strong-conflict veto

Skip a gold buy only when completed-bar DXY momentum is strongly positive; skip a gold sell only when it is strongly negative. Missing or stale features leave the original trade unchanged. Higher win rate alone is not an improvement if net returns, drawdown, costs or trade count deteriorate.

Secondary diagnostic: require an inverse gold/DXY return correlation

The same conflict veto operates only when the latest paired hourly gold/DXY log-return correlation is ≤ −0.25. It needs at least 100 of the latest 120 paired observations within ten calendar days, with its latest paired endpoint no more than one hour old. This is one predeclared diagnostic, not a winner selected after looking at results and not evidence of untouched out-of-sample success.

Entry features & vetoed-trade breakdown

Dates are UTC; risk-normalized P&L includes the selected cost scenario. Positive vetoed P&L is profit forgone; negative vetoed P&L is loss avoided. No later entry made possible by skipping a trade is recovered here.

Exact predeclared rules, native source settings & data provenance

How the filter works

  • H1 times are bar opens. A close becomes available only after open + 3,600 seconds, at or before the original EA entry.
  • Use four consecutive hourly closes for a three-clock-hour DXY log return. Latest usable close must be no more than one hour old.
  • Strong momentum threshold = √3 × sample standard deviation of the previous 120 valid hourly DXY log returns. The normalizer ends before the three-hour signal block; all observations must lie within the previous ten calendar days.
  • Veto long if momentum ≥ threshold; veto short if momentum ≤ −threshold. Weak or opposing dollar momentum leaves the entry unchanged.
  • No zero-fill, price forward-fill or nearest/future matching. Missing, stale or insufficient history passes the original trade and is counted.

Normalization & dates

  • Only trades entered on/after the selected UTC start and naturally closed before the end-exclusive date are included. Pre-window carried positions and native test-end liquidations are excluded.
  • NetR = original per-lot gross + commission + swap, divided by original filled initial-stop risk per lot. P&L = NetR × $100.
  • All five EA positions are combined chronologically at close. No account risk allocation, overlapping-exposure cap or equity guard is imposed.
  • Cost stress adds $0.10 gold-price cost on each side ($20 per one-lot round trip) and doubles recorded negative swap. Native entries and exits do not change.
  • Daily closed-return Sharpe uses all UTC calendar days and √365. It is not a tick-equity Sharpe; nonpositive balance makes it unavailable.

Exact frozen study plan


Limits before any adoption:
  • This entry-veto screen cannot recover counterfactual later signals after skipped positions; full native filter-on/filter-off reruns are required.
  • Historical gold sources are Exness Trial16, with only 15% real ticks globally; real-tick coverage begins in January 2026. DXY and gold correlation features come from Trial15. Cross-feed differences can affect synchronization.
  • Broker DXY CFD is not an official ICE spot/futures series. Filter returns are not proof that DXY moves first or causes gold moves.
  • These strategies and dates have been researched before. The last two years are a reporting slice, not a genuinely untouched out-of-sample validation.
  • Sample size, filtering concentration and shared gold exposure matter. No live bots, account settings, charts, installers, BATs or global website pages changed.
